label: early-position (t=3-5) conjunction of specific early tokens (c/x first, 3/h/e/p)
explanation: Very sparse (0.07% of steps). Fires almost only at steps 3-5 (about 94% of activation mass): the 4th to 6th original tokens, or the <DEL> step when L is 3-5. It never fires at t=0-2 and almost never in the copy phase. Within that window it depends on which tokens came first, in a graded, distributed way: first token c or x (lift about 7x), 3/h/e two steps back (up to 11x), and 3/p/y/j one step back (up to 8x). The top activations are sequences like c x 3 / c 3 h / c 3 3 at the <DEL> step. No boolean conjunction captures this well. The best simple predicate (t in 3-5, first token c/x, and 3/h/e two back or 3/p one back) gets dev F1 0.16 and mass recall 0.36; tighter conjunctions reach precision 0.35 but recall 0.16. It looks like a soft linear threshold over the first few tokens of hidden state rather than a nameable token or position rule. Magnitude is higher at <DEL> after short c/x-initial sequences, but I did not check this beyond the top examples.
